title: A Measurement Plane for Quantum Networking
authors: Abderrahim Amlou, Amar Abane, Anouar Rahmouni, Mheni Merzouki, Abdella Battou, Ahmed Lbath, Ya-Shian Li-Baboud, Oliver Slattery, Thomas Gerrits
abstract: Quantum networking testbeds lack a distinct plane for coordinating distributed measurements and collecting experimental data across heterogeneous devices. To address this gap, we present the Measurement Plane, a dedicated plane that complements the data, control, and management planes rather than replacing or extending their pipelines. The contribution is presented as a distributed framework that organizes measurement functions into four layers: application, experiment coordination, capability, and resource agents. Our design separates user workflows from device-specific control.   We implemented the framework as containerized microservices connected through publish--subscribe messaging, and validated it on a two-node quantum networking setup connected by an optical network. The framework successfully coordinated remote nodes to execute coincidence measurement and polarization entanglement distribution experiments with visibility interference of up to 98 percent. This evaluation demonstrated the effectiveness of the framework for supporting complex, distributed quantum experiments, enabling online measurement and feedback, and significantly reducing manual configuration and execution effort.
summary: The paper introduces the Measurement Plane, a modular, distributed framework designed to standardize and automate data collection across heterogeneous quantum networking testbeds. By separating user workflows from low-level hardware control into distinct software layers, it enables complex, multi-step quantum experiments remotely. This significantly reduces manual configuration effort while maintaining high experimental fidelity.
main_problem: Quantum networking testbeds lack a distinct, standardized plane for coordinating distributed measurements and collecting experimental data across heterogeneous quantum devices.
main_result: The proposed Measurement Plane successfully coordinated remote nodes to execute complex experiments like coincidence measurement and polarization entanglement distribution with high visibility (up to 98%).
method: A distributed framework using containerized microservices connected via publish-subscribe messaging was implemented, organizing functions into four distinct layers.
model_or_system: The system is a software architecture designed for quantum networking testbeds, involving two remote nodes (Alice and Bob) connected by an optical network. It separates user workflows from device-specific control using capability abstraction.
key_observables: Visibility interference of up to 98% in polarization entanglement distribution; coincidence detection peaks at zero delay.
important_parameters: Two-node quantum networking setup; $\approx 1.4$ km optical fiber link.
main_assumptions: The architecture assumes communication via a shared messaging infrastructure (NATS) and demonstrates feasibility rather than ultimate scale limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the layered architecture, the measurement lifecycle (Submission to Completion), the identifier hierarchy used for tracking, and experimental results showing coincidence histograms and polarization fringe visibility.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Measurement Plane concept, details its multi-layered distributed microservice architecture (Application $ightarrow$ Coordination $ightarrow$ Capability $ightarrow$ Resource Agent), describes the identification scheme, and validates it through automated execution of remote quantum experiments.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial software infrastructure layer for realizing complex quantum network protocols, abstracting away device heterogeneity which is a major bottleneck in experimental quantum information science.
